Existing SourceRecordId ordinal equality and mapping publication identity remain exact.
owners.invariant: One exact tenant/source-key/namespace authority serializes batch admission and durable source-record mapping publication. Complete verified published-batch order and frozen SourceClaims define mutable replace/remove mappings; source revision/generation fences stale plans and omissions. owners.mustPreserve: Freeze complete rows and expected revisions. No partial batch visibility. Target owner replay uses accepted native facts without live coordinator lookup. Staged observation and execution share one ApplicationImportBatch revision; old ImportBatch is a cutover predecessor only.

owners.selectedIdentity: Tenant + exact directed source application / relationship kind / target application tuple under its unchanged existing UUIDv5 IdFor. Supplied RelationshipId must equal this tuple identity; it is not an arbitrary caller UUID. Source and target direction is significant; accepted EV-D03/EV-D04 remove any separate tuple claim/release owner.
owners.invariant: One exact directed source/kind/target relationship lifecycle with unchanged deterministic UUIDv5 tuple identity; active endpoint/source-visibility and exact source/target revision guards remain. No independent tuple claim/release authority is introduced.
owners.mustPreserve: Retirement requires an approved successor for exact app revision; import holds block incompatible local change.

owners.declaredIdentity: Tenant / artifact-disclosures / DisclosureId; changed initial intent conflicts; logical expectedRevision on delivery/revoke; approval/delivery compare server timestamps for retries. Portia appends against the hydrated physical stream position; a logical revision does not create another physical boundary.
owners.selectedIdentity: Tenant / artifact-disclosures / DisclosureId, with exact artifact content, handling-policy revision and recipient/purpose binding. Selected mutations use CommandId.
owners.invariant: One disclosure binds immutable artifact content, handling-policy revision, recipient and purpose; delivery requires that approved identity and revocation is final.
owners.boundaryRationale: Separating approval from delivery without a one-use approval authorization could deliver changed content or a different recipient. These three monotonic states fit together.

owners.declaredIdentity: Tenant / artifact-dispositions / dispositionId; explicit revision; result handler binds execution-event ID and attempt number; approval retry includes ApprovedAt. Portia appends against the hydrated physical stream position; a logical revision does not create another physical boundary.
owners.selectedIdentity: Tenant / artifact-dispositions / DispositionId, with exact approved content and execution attempt identity. Selected mutations use CommandId.
owners.invariant: Only an approved exact source with elapsed retention/no active holds or reliance may start execution; one outstanding attempt; disposed result is terminal and yields tombstone.
owners.boundaryRationale: Approval and execution need an explicit durable authorization token and one outstanding executor claim if separated; the lifetime attempt history itself is unnecessary to that rule.

owners.declaredIdentity: tenant / artifact-qualified derived receiving GrantId; caller root CommandId remains distinct
owners.selectedIdentity: UUIDv5 namespace ArtifactId, UTF8 artifact-download-grant:v1:{canonical TenantId}:{canonical CommandId}. Receiving root additionally verifies exact artifact/command/original-actor tuple. No generic operation lookup.
owners.invariant: One exact receiving grant owns the authenticated encrypted original artifact ticket/result after EvidenceArtifact first admitted and pinned availability with frozen202. Complete required held source uses and exact issue DecisionAt precede native issued-v2; cancellation fences delayed issuance and terminal proofs settle all uses. Original expiry never renews under the same root identity. Existing artifact-issued v1 decoder remains read-only compatibility.
